result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B uses its terms more consistently (Member, Tool, Due back). Its helper text sets up the desk cases, such as 'Only tools on the shelf can be lent' and 'Enter a tool to see who has it', and it labels the 7-day default due date as a default. However, B states an unconfirmed 'Up to 30 days' limit and shows stock counts at the top. A mixes 'lend/check out/take back/check in/return by/due/out on loan', shows a pre-filled due date with no default label, and gives no visible messages for the problem cases. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A splits the screen cleanly into Lend and Return panels and keeps its terms mostly consistent (member, tool, due back). It labels the due date as a default, but it also invents a 30-day maximum and shows inventory totals across the top. B is a practical desk layout with a list of tools out on loan and quick check-in, but its terms drift (lend / check out / take back / check in, return by / due), its default due date isn't labeled as a default, and its date is hardcoded. Neither screenshot shows the member-not-found, tool-already-out or nothing-lent messages.
